conditions: when the accent kernel is on an open syllable

entailment.quote: When the accent kernel is on an open syllable, there is a tendency to prolong the vowel.

anchor.exact: Usually one of the first two syllables carries the accent. If the first syllable is closed it will generally receive the accent, but if it is open, the second syllable will have the accent.

statement.en: Usually one of the first two syllables carries the pitch accent: if the first syllable is closed, it generally receives the accent, but if it is open, the second syllable receives the accent.
statement.ja: 通常、最初の2音節のいずれかがアクセントを担い、第1音節が閉音節であれば一般にアクセントを受け、開音節であれば第2音節がアクセントを受ける。

entailment.quote: Usually one of the first two syllables carries the accent. If the first syllable is closed it will generally receive the accent, but if it is open, the second syllable will have the accent.

anchor.exact: There are only a few minimal pairs, i.e. words where accent is the only indication of semantic difference

statement.en: There are only a few minimal pairs where accent is the only indication of semantic difference.

entailment.quote: There are only a few minimal pairs, i.e. words where accent is the only indication of semantic difference

anchor.exact: Sentence intonation is slightly falling in declarative sentences

statement.en: Sentence intonation is slightly falling in declarative sentences.
statement.ja: 平叙文における文イントネーションはわずかに下降する。

anchor.exact: and gradually rising in questions.

anchor.exact: However, the use of sentence final particles/forms (see section 14.11) greatly diminishes the importance of intonation.

entailment.quote: the use of sentence final particles/forms (see section 14.11) greatly diminishes the importance of intonation

anchor.exact:
The word classes of Ainu are initially divided into the following three major groups:

        Nominals
        Verbals
        Clitics

statement.en: The word classes of Ainu are initially divided into three major groups: Nominals, Verbals, and Clitics.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の品詞は、まず名詞類、動詞類、接語類の3大グループに区分される。

entailment.quote: The word classes of Ainu are initially divided into the following three major groups: Nominals Verbals Clitics

anchor.exact: they are defined as "free forms, which cannot be predicates".

statement.en: Nominals are defined as free forms that cannot be predicates.
statement.ja: 名詞類は、述語になり得ない自由形式として定義される。

entailment.quote: they are defined as 'free forms, which cannot be predicates'

anchor.exact: General nouns are defined as forms which may be sentence subject or object and which may be followed by case postpositions.

statement.en: General nouns can function as sentence subject or object and may be followed by case postpositions.
statement.ja: 普通名詞は文の主語または目的語になり得、格後置詞の後続を受けることができる。

entailment.quote: General nouns are defined as forms which may be sentence subject or object and which may be followed by case postpositions.

anchor.exact: Furthermore, they may be preceded by adnouns and adnominalized sentences, and some may take noun suffixes and/or noun prefixes.

statement.en: General nouns may be preceded by adnouns and adnominalized sentences, and some may take noun suffixes and/or noun prefixes.
statement.ja: 普通名詞は連体詞や連体節の先行を受けることができ、一部は名詞接尾辞や名詞接頭辞を取り得る。

entailment.quote: they may be preceded by adnouns and adnominalized sentences, and some may take noun suffixes and/or noun prefixes

anchor.exact: Those that may be inalienably possessed may appear with pronominal affixes as well and form "the belonging form" (see 12.1.1).

statement.en: General nouns that can be inalienably possessed may appear with pronominal affixes to form the belonging form.
statement.ja: 不可譲譲渡可能な普通名詞は、代名詞的接辞を伴って「所属形」を形成し得る。

entailment.quote: Those that may be inalienably possessed may appear with pronominal affixes as well and form "the belonging form"

anchor.exact: proper names (toponyms and personal names) may appear in the same roles as general nouns, but they can take no prefixes or suffixes

statement.en: Proper names can take no prefixes or suffixes.
statement.ja: 固有名詞は接頭辞も接尾辞も取ることができない。

entailment.quote: they can take no prefixes or suffixes

anchor.exact: they are only in extremely rare cases preceded by an adnoun or an adnominalized sentence.

statement.en: Proper names are only in extremely rare cases preceded by an adnoun or an adnominalized sentence.
statement.ja: 固有名詞が連体詞や連体節の先行を受けるのは極めて稀な場合に限られる。

entailment.quote: they are only in extremely rare cases preceded by an adnoun or an adnominalized sentence

anchor.exact: Only the first and the second person have pronouns, and they have both singular and plural forms.

statement.en: Only the first and second persons have personal pronouns, having both singular and plural forms.
statement.ja: 人称代名詞を有するのは1人称と2人称のみであり、それぞれ単数形と複数形が存在する。

entailment.quote: Only the first and the second person have pronouns, and they have both singular and plural forms

anchor.exact: Syntactically they behave like general nouns and proper names, but their use is restricted to situations of emphasis. Ordinarily, pronominal affixes (see 14.10) take their place.

statement.en: Personal pronouns behave syntactically like general nouns and proper names, but their use is restricted to situations of emphasis.
statement.ja: 人称代名詞は統語的には普通名詞や固有名詞と同様に振る舞うが、その使用は強調の状況に限られる。

entailment.quote: Syntactically they behave like general nouns and proper names, but their use is restricted to situations of emphasis

anchor.exact: Apart from the indefinites, they all have adnominal forms which belong in the class of clitics under the subclass of adnouns (see 14.1).

statement.en: Apart from the indefinites, anaphorics, demonstratives, and interrogatives all have adnominal forms that belong to the subclass of adnouns under clitics.
statement.ja: 不定詞を除き、前照応詞、指示詞、疑問詞はいずれも接語類の下位区分である連体詞に属する連体形をもつ。

entailment.quote: Apart from the indefinites, they all have adnominal forms which belong in the class of clitics under the subclass of adnouns

anchor.exact: All except the anaphorics have adverbial forms which do fall under the class of nominals, but belong in subclass 6: Conjunctions, Interjections, and Adverbs.

statement.en: All pronominal nouns except the anaphorics have adverbial forms that fall under nominals in the subclass of Conjunctions, Interjections, and Adverbs.
statement.ja: 前照応詞以外のすべての代名名詞は、名詞類の下位区分である「接続詞、感動詞、副詞」に属する副詞形をもつ。

entailment.quote: All except the anaphorics have adverbial forms which do fall under the class of nominals, but belong in subclass 6: Conjunctions, Interjections, and Adverbs

anchor.exact: This subclass comprises numerals and quantity expressions.

statement.en: The subclass of quantity nouns comprises numerals and quantity expressions.
statement.ja: 数量名詞の下位区分は、数詞および数量表現から構成される。

entailment.quote: This subclass comprises numerals and quantity expressions.

anchor.exact: Positionals are frequently tied to a general noun which pinpoints the locative reference for the positional, and in such constructions they cannot quite be considered "free forms".

statement.en: Positionals are frequently tied to a general noun specifying their locative reference, and in such constructions they cannot quite be considered free forms.
statement.ja: 位置名詞はその所在指示を特定する普通名詞と結びつくことが多く、そのような構文では完全に自由形式とは見なし得ない。

entailment.quote: Positionals are frequently tied to a general noun which pinpoints the locative reference for the positional, and in such constructions they cannot quite be considered "free forms".

anchor.exact: Nevertheless, they do occasionally occur in isola-

statement.en: Positionals occasionally occur in isolation.
statement.ja: 位置名詞は時折、単独（孤立形）で生起することがある。

entailment.quote: Nevertheless, they do occasionally occur in isolation

anchor.exact: All of them are free forms which syntactically function as adverbial adjuncts. They modify a sentence or a verb expression, but cannot be relational adjuncts

statement.en: Conjunctions, interjections, and adverbs are all free forms that function syntactically as adverbial adjuncts modifying a sentence or verb expression, and cannot serve as relational adjuncts.
statement.ja: 接続詞・感動詞・副詞はいずれも文や動詞表現を修飾する副詞的付加語として統語的に機能する自立形式であり、関係付加語になることはできない。

entailment.quote: All of them are free forms which syntactically function as adverbial adjuncts. They modify a sentence or a verb expression, but cannot be relational adjuncts

anchor.exact: Verbals, which are described in detail in chapter 13, are here defined as "forms which can be predicates".

statement.en: Verbals are defined as forms that can function as predicates.
statement.ja: 動詞類は述語になりうる形式として定義される。

entailment.quote: Verbals, which are described in detail in chapter 13, are here defined as "forms which can be predicates".

anchor.exact: Subclassification of the verbals first single out the copula, ne, which cannot form a sentence by itself, but is always connected to a noun expression

statement.en: The copula ne cannot form a sentence by itself and is always connected to a noun expression.
statement.ja: コピュラ ne は単独で文を形成することはできず、常に名詞表現と結合している。

entailment.quote: the copula, ne, which cannot form a sentence by itself, but is always connected to a noun expression

anchor.exact: A small group of verbs which for semantic reasons never combine with pronominal affixes and never take any other subject or object. These verbs are also closed to affixation of verb prefixes and verb suffixes

statement.en: Closed verbs are a small group of verbs that for semantic reasons never combine with pronominal affixes, never take any other subject or object, and do not accept verb prefixes or suffixes.
statement.ja: 閉鎖動詞は意味的理由から代名接辞と結合せず、他の主語や目的語もとらず、動詞接頭辞や接尾辞の付加も受けない少数の動詞群である。

entailment.quote: A small group of verbs which for semantic reasons never combine with pronominal affixes and never take any other subject or object. These verbs are also closed to affixation of verb prefixes and verb suffixes

anchor.exact: These verbs never combine with pronominal affixes in the objective case, and they never take any other object either.

statement.en: Intransitive verbs never combine with objective pronominal affixes and never take any other object.
statement.ja: 自動詞は目的格の代名接辞と結合することは決してなく、他のいかなる目的語もとらない。

entailment.quote: These verbs never combine with pronominal affixes in the objective case, and they never take any other object either.

anchor.exact: Within this group are also found a number of verbs which in meaning correspond to adjectives in other languages (see 13.3.1). "Adjectives" are not set up as a separate word class in the present analysis.

statement.en: Forms corresponding semantically to adjectives in other languages are treated as a subset of intransitive verbs, and 'adjectives' are not recognized as a separate word class.
statement.ja: 他言語の形容詞に意味的に対応する形式は自動詞の一部として扱われ、「形容詞」は独立した品詞として立てられない。

entailment.quote: Within this group are also found a number of verbs which in meaning correspond to adjectives in other languages (see 13.3.1). "Adjectives" are not set up as a separate word class in the present analysis.

anchor.exact: The transitive verbs can combine pronominal affixes in both the nominative and the objective case, and they can take noun expressions as their objects as well.

statement.en: Transitive verbs can combine with pronominal affixes in both the nominative and the objective cases, and can take noun expressions as objects.
statement.ja: 他動詞は主格および目的格の代名接辞の双方と結合でき、名詞表現を目的語にとることもできる。

entailment.quote: The transitive verbs can combine pronominal affixes in both the nominative and the objective case, and they can take noun expressions as their objects as well.

anchor.exact: Actually only very few transitive verbs may appear without an overt object, except when the object is the third person, which has no pronominal affix

statement.en: Very few transitive verbs may appear without an overt object, except when the object is third person, which has no overt pronominal affix.
statement.ja: 目的語が三人称（代名接辞をもたない）である場合を除き、明示的な目的語を伴わずに現れうる他動詞はごくわずかである。

conditions: except when the object is third person

entailment.quote: Actually only very few transitive verbs may appear without an overt object, except when the object is the third person, which has no pronominal affix (see 14.10).

anchor.exact: Both transitive and intransitive verbs may be shifted back and forth between these two categories by the addition or removal of one or more verb prefixes and/or verb suffixes.

statement.en: Verbs can shift between transitive and intransitive categories through the addition or removal of verbal prefixes or suffixes.
statement.ja: 動詞は、1つ以上の動詞接頭辞や接尾辞の付加または除去によって、他動詞と自動詞のカテゴリー間を往復して移行させることができる。

entailment.quote: Both transitive and intransitive verbs may be shifted back and forth between these two categories by the addition or removal of one or more verb prefixes and/or verb suffixes.

anchor.exact: Clitics are described in detail in chapter 14. They form a large, heterogenous class of bound forms, and their only shared characteristic is that of being unable to appear independently as predicates or as isolated adjuncts to predicates.

statement.en: Clitics are bound forms characterized by an inability to appear independently as predicates or as isolated adjuncts to predicates.
statement.ja: 接語類（クリティック）は、述語として、あるいは述語に対する単独の付加語として自立して現れることができないという共通特徴をもつ結合形式である。

entailment.quote: They form a large, heterogenous class of bound forms, and their only shared characteristic is that of being unable to appear independently as predicates or as isolated adjuncts to predicates.

anchor.exact: Both of these precede and modify nominals, but noun prefixes are more tightly bound to the forms they precede than adnouns.

statement.en: Both adnouns and noun prefixes precede and modify nominals, but noun prefixes are more tightly bound to their hosts than adnouns.
statement.ja: 副名詞と名詞接頭辞はいずれも名詞類に先行してそれを修飾するが、名詞接頭辞は副名詞よりも後続形式に対して緊密に結合している。

entailment.quote: Both of these precede and modify nominals, but noun prefixes are more tightly bound to the forms they precede than adnouns.

anchor.exact: Noun prefixes are a very small group of morphemes, which predominantly have to do with direction, and which are therefore mainly used with positionals or general nouns denoting location.

statement.en: Noun prefixes are a very small set of morphemes predominantly expressing direction, and are primarily used with positionals or general nouns denoting location.
statement.ja: 名詞接頭辞は主として方向に関わるごく少数の形態素のグループであり、そのため主に位置名詞や場所を表す一般名詞とともに用いられる。

entailment.quote: Noun prefixes are a very small group of morphemes, which predominantly have to do with direction, and which are therefore mainly used with positionals or general nouns denoting location.

anchor.exact: Adnouns only precede general nouns; the majority are anaphoric, deictic, or interrogative, but there are a number of other adnouns as well

statement.en: Adnouns only precede general nouns, and the majority of them are anaphoric, deictic, or interrogative.
statement.ja: 副名詞は一般名詞にのみ先行し、その大部分は前方照応的、直示的、あるいは疑問的である。

entailment.quote: Adnouns only precede general nouns; the majority are anaphoric, deictic, or interrogative, but there are a number of other adnouns as well (see 14.1.1).

anchor.exact: This group consists of only three morphemes, two of which follow general nouns, while the third follows positionals. They all serve to extend or modify the meaning of the form which they follow

statement.en: Noun suffixes consist of only three morphemes: two follow general nouns, while the third follows positionals, all serving to extend or modify the meaning of the host.
statement.ja: 名詞接尾辞はわずか3個の形態素からなり、2個は一般名詞に後続し、3個目は位置名詞に後続して、いずれも先行する形式の意味を拡張または修飾する働きをする。

entailment.quote: This group consists of only three morphemes, two of which follow general nouns, while the third follows positionals. They all serve to extend or modify the meaning of the form which they follow

anchor.exact: The attributive postpositions are added to a noun in order to enable it to modify a subsequent noun

statement.en: Attributive postpositions are added to a noun in order to enable it to modify a subsequent noun.
statement.ja: 連体後置詞は、名詞に後続の名詞を修飾させるために名詞に付加される。

entailment.quote: The attributive postpositions are added to a noun in order to enable it to modify a subsequent noun

anchor.exact: The morphemes in this group are placed between nouns or noun expressions of equal weight to express enumeration of the forms involved.

statement.en: Coordinative postpositions are placed between nouns or noun expressions of equal weight to express enumeration.
statement.ja: 並列後置詞は、並置関係を表すために等位の名詞または名詞表現の間に置かれる。

entailment.quote: The morphemes in this group are placed between nouns or noun expressions of equal weight to express enumeration of the forms involved

anchor.exact: Follow nominals and noun expressions to mark them as relational adjuncts (see 15.4).

statement.en: Case postpositions follow nominals and noun expressions to mark them as relational adjuncts.
statement.ja: 格後置詞は体言および名詞表現に後続し、それらを関係副加語として標識する。

entailment.quote: Case Postpositions Follow nominals and noun expressions to mark them as relational adjuncts

anchor.exact: All nominals, except the last group (conjunctions, interjections, and adverbs) may be followed by case postpositions.

statement.en: All nominals except conjunctions, interjections, and adverbs may be followed by case postpositions.
statement.ja: 接続詞、間投詞、副詞を除くすべての体言は格後置詞を伴うことができる。

entailment.quote: All nominals, except the last group (conjunctions, interjections, and adverbs) may be followed by case postpositions

anchor.exact: However, as shown in section 14.5, not all "cases" are marked with postpositions.

statement.en: Not all cases are marked with postpositions.
statement.ja: すべての「格」が後置詞で標識されるわけではない。

entailment.quote: not all "cases" are marked with postpositions

statement.en: Restrictive postpositions may follow all types of nominals, noun expressions, and clitics such as case postpositions, conjunctionalizers, and nominalizers without altering their syntactical role.
statement.ja: 限定後置詞はあらゆる種類の体言、名詞表現のほか、格後置詞・接続詞化辞・名詞化辞といった接語にも後続でき、その統語的役割を変えない。

entailment.quote: The restrictive postpositions may follow not only nominals of all types and noun expressions, but also other clitics such as case postpositions, conjunctionalizers ... and nominalizers ... They do not alter the syntactical role or status of

anchor.exact: pronominal prefixes in the nominative case may connect with certain general nouns, when inalienable possession is expressed (see 12.1.2).

statement.en: Pronominal prefixes in the nominative case may attach to certain general nouns to express inalienable possession.
statement.ja: 主格の人称接頭辞は、不可譲渡的所有を表す際に特定の一般名詞に接続することがある。

entailment.quote: pronominal prefixes in the nominative case may connect with certain general nouns, when inalienable possession is expressed

anchor.exact: Furthermore, pronominal prefixes in the objective case may connect with positionals.

statement.en: Pronominal prefixes in the objective case may attach to positionals.
statement.ja: 目的格の人称接頭辞は位置詞に接続することができる。

entailment.quote: pronominal prefixes in the objective case may connect with positionals

anchor.exact: The verb prefixes attach directly to transitive and intransitive verbs, and one verb may have a number of prefixes attached (see 14.7.4).

statement.en: Verb prefixes attach directly to transitive and intransitive verbs, and a single verb may take multiple prefixes.
statement.ja: 動詞接頭辞は他動詞および自動詞に直接接続し、1つの動詞に複数の接頭辞が付くことがある。

entailment.quote: The verb prefixes attach directly to transitive and intransitive verbs, and one verb may have a number of prefixes attached

anchor.exact: There are three types of verb prefixes: intensifying prefixes, which do not affect the grammatical properties of the verb (see 14.7.1); "adjunct-reducing prefixes", which turn transitive verbs into intransitive verbs

statement.en: Verb prefixes comprise three types: intensifying prefixes, adjunct-reducing prefixes (transitive to intransitive), and adjunct-increasing prefixes (intransitive to transitive).
statement.ja: 動詞接頭辞には3種類あり、強意接頭辞、副加語削減接頭辞（他動詞から自動詞へ）、副加語増加接頭辞（自動詞から他動詞へ）である。

entailment.quote: There are three types of verb prefixes: intensifying prefixes, ...; "adjunct-reducing prefixes", which turn transitive verbs into intransitive verbs, ...; and "adjunct-increasing prefixes", which ... turn intransitive verbs into transitive

anchor.exact: Like the verb prefixes, the suffixes attach to transitive and intransitive verbs, and they may be subdivided into the same three groups.

statement.en: Verb suffixes attach to transitive and intransitive verbs and comprise adjunct-neutral suffixes, one adjunct-reducing suffix, and adjunct-increasing suffixes.
statement.ja: 動詞接尾辞は他動詞および自動詞に接続し、副加語中立接尾辞、単一の副加語削減接尾辞、副加語増加接尾辞に細分される。

entailment.quote: the suffixes attach to transitive and intransitive verbs, and they may be subdivided into the same three groups. ... There is only one "adjunct-reducing suffix", which turns transitive verbs into intransitive verbs ... "Adjunct-increasing s

anchor.exact: There is only one "adjunct-reducing suffix", which turns transitive verbs into intransitive verbs (see 14.8.2).

statement.en: There is only one adjunct-reducing suffix, which turns transitive verbs into intransitive verbs.
statement.ja: 他動詞を自動詞に変える副加語削減接尾辞は1つしか存在しない。

entailment.quote: There is only one "adjunct-reducing suffix", which turns transitive verbs into intransitive verbs

anchor.exact: "Adjunct-increasing suffixes" either perform the opposite function, namely to turn intransitive verbs into transitive verbs, or they express the causative (see 14.8.3).

statement.en: Adjunct-increasing suffixes either turn intransitive verbs into transitive verbs or express the causative.
statement.ja: 副加語増加接尾辞は、自動詞を他動詞に変えるか、使役を表す。

entailment.quote: "Adjunct-increasing suffixes" either perform the opposite function, namely to turn intransitive verbs into transitive verbs, or they express the causative

anchor.exact: This entails that only forms which are capable of being removed from the verb to which they are attached by the interpolation of verb suffixes and/or a pronominal suffix qualify as auxiliaries.

statement.en: Only forms that can be separated from the verb by the interpolation of verb suffixes and/or a pronominal suffix qualify as verb auxiliaries.
statement.ja: 動詞接尾辞や人称接尾辞の挿入によって接続動詞から隔てられる形態素のみが動詞補助辞とみなされる。

entailment.quote: only forms which are capable of being removed from the verb to which they are attached by the interpolation of verb suffixes and/or a pronominal suffix qualify as auxiliaries

anchor.exact: They are placed before verb prefixes and after verb suffixes, but before verb auxiliaries.

statement.en: Pronominal affixes attach to verbs or verb expressions before verb prefixes and after verb suffixes, but before verb auxiliaries.

entailment.quote: The pronominal affixes are pre- or suffixed to verbs ... or verb expressions ... They are placed before verb prefixes and after verb suffixes, but before verb auxiliaries

anchor.exact: Three kinds of grammatical person are expressed by pronominal affixes, namely the 1st, the 2nd, and the indefinite person.

statement.en: Pronominal affixes express three grammatical persons: first person, second person, and indefinite person.

entailment.quote: Three kinds of grammatical person are expressed by pronominal affixes, namely the 1st, the 2nd, and the indefinite person.

anchor.exact: Mode of action, aspect and modality are expressed by a variety of auxiliaries which are added to the verb in its extended form.

anchor.exact: Predicates are usually negated with the adverbs somo, "not", and iteke, "don't!"

anchor.exact: Verbs which never combine with a pronominal affix form a group by themselves, the closed or non-affixing verbs⁴².

entailment.quote: Verbs which never combine with a pronominal affix form a group by themselves, the closed or non-affixing verbs.

anchor.exact: They do not combine with verb prefixes or suffixes either, and they only appear with some of the auxiliaries.

entailment.quote: They do not combine with verb prefixes or suffixes either, and they only appear with some of the auxiliaries.

anchor.exact: Characteristically the verbs in this group are terms for natural phenomena or for acts with no specific agent, but a few stative verbs also belong here.

statement.en: Closed verbs are characteristically terms for natural phenomena or for acts with no specific agent, but a few stative verbs also belong to this group.

statement.ja: 過程が期待通りあるいは望み通りに遂行されず何かが欠けていることを表す不全的動作様相は、補助動詞 niwkes および orakse によって表される。

entailment.quote: This is expressed by the auxiliaries niwkes and orakse.

anchor.exact: Niwkes simply indicates that part of a process has been left undone, although it should have been done, but orakse furthermore adds a nuance of dissatisfaction or lack of fulfilment: the part that is lacking is a source of discomfort for the subject.

statement.en: The auxiliary niwkes simply indicates that part of a process has been left undone although it should have been done, whereas orakse adds a nuance of dissatisfaction or discomfort for the subject regarding the lacking part.
statement.ja: 補助動詞 niwkes はなされるべき過程の一部が未完了のまま残されたことのみを示すのに対し、orakse はさらにその欠けている部分が主体にとって不快や不満の源であるというニュアンスを加える。

entailment.quote: Niwkes simply indicates that part of a process has been left undone, although it should have been done, but orakse furthermore adds a nuance of dissatisfaction or lack of fulfilment: the part that is lacking is a source of discomfort for th

anchor.exact: The form marking the imperfective aspect is the conjunctionalizer wa, followed by the existential verb, an (sg.) / oka (pl.).

statement.en: The imperfective aspect is marked by the conjunctionalizer wa followed by the existential verb an (singular) or oka (plural).
statement.ja: 非完了アスペクトは、接続詞化辞 wa に存在動詞 an（単数）/ oka（複数）が後続することによって標示される。

entailment.quote: The form marking the imperfective aspect is the conjunctionalizer wa, followed by the existential verb, an (sg.) / oka (pl.).

anchor.exact: The restrictive post position patek may be interpolated between wa and an to indicate that the subject is doing something to the exclusion of everything else.

statement.en: The restrictive postposition patek may be interpolated between wa and an to indicate that the subject performs an action to the exclusion of everything else.
statement.ja: 限定の後置詞 patek を wa と an の間に挿入することで、主語が他のすべてを排除してその動作だけを行っていることを表すことができる。

entailment.quote: The restrictive post position patek may be interpolated between wa and an to indicate that the subject is doing something to the exclusion of everything else.

anchor.exact: Occasionally the imperfective aspect is formed with the conjunctionalizers hine or no instead of wa.

statement.en: The imperfective aspect is occasionally formed with the conjunctionalizers hine or no instead of wa.
statement.ja: 非完了アスペクトは、wa の代わりに接続詞化辞 hine または no を用いて形成されることもある。

entailment.quote: Occasionally the imperfective aspect is formed with the conjunctionalizers hine or no instead of wa.

anchor.exact: The completed aspect is marked with the verb okere (sg.) / okerpa (pl.), "finish".

statement.en: The completed aspect is marked by the verb okere (singular) or okerpa (plural) 'finish'.
statement.ja: 完了したアスペクト（completed aspect）は、動詞 okere（単数）/ okerpa（複数）「終える」によって標示される。

entailment.quote: The completed aspect is marked with the verb okere (sg.) / okerpa (pl.), "finish".

anchor.exact: Usually the conjunctionalizer wa, precedes okere, but there are examples of okere being attached directly to the main verb.

statement.en: The conjunctionalizer wa usually precedes okere, but okere can also attach directly to the main verb.
statement.ja: 通常は接続詞化辞 wa が okere に先行するが、okere が本動詞に直接付加される例もある。

entailment.quote: Usually the conjunctionalizer wa, precedes okere, but there are examples of okere being attached directly to the main verb.

anchor.exact: The uncompleted aspect indicates simultaneity between a process and the temporal frame maintained by the speaker.

statement.en: The uncompleted aspect indicates simultaneity between a process and the temporal frame maintained by the speaker.
statement.ja: 未完結アスペクト（uncompleted aspect）は、プロセスと話者が維持する時間枠との同時性を示す。

entailment.quote: The uncompleted aspect indicates simultaneity between a process and the temporal frame maintained by the speaker.

anchor.exact: When verb expressions with kane an/oka, or with the imperfective aspect marking wa an/oka, have a pronominal affix as their subject, not only the main verb, but also the auxiliary will usually carry the affix.

statement.en: When verbal expressions with kane an/oka or wa an/oka have a pronominal affix as their subject, the affix is usually marked on both the main verb and the auxiliary.
statement.ja: kane an/oka や wa an/oka を伴う動詞表現が代名接辞を主語とする場合、本動詞だけでなく補助動詞にも通常その接辞が付加される。

conditions: when the subject is indexed by a pronominal affix

entailment.quote: When verb expressions with kane an/oka, or with the imperfective aspect marking wa an/oka, have a pronominal affix as their subject, not only the main verb, but also the auxiliary will usually carry the affix.

anchor.exact: The restrictive postposition patek, may - like with wa an - be interpolated between kane and an as well. The meaning is to concentrate upon doing one thing only.

statement.en: The restrictive postposition patek may be interpolated between kane and an to express concentrating upon doing one thing only.
statement.ja: 限定の後置詞 patek は kane と an の間にも挿入することができ、一つのことだけを行うことに集中しているという意味を表す。

entailment.quote: The restrictive postposition patek, may - like with wa an - be interpolated between kane and an as well. The meaning is to concentrate upon doing one thing only.

anchor.exact: Other dialects, such as for instance the Saru dialect, have kor an in a function corresponding to that of kane an in the Shizunai dialect, and the contemporal conjunctionalizer in these dialects is also kor instead of kane

statement.en: In other dialects such as Saru, kor an corresponds in function to Shizunai kane an, and the contemporal conjunctionalizer is kor instead of kane.
statement.ja: 沙流方言などの他の方言では、静内方言の kane an に対応する機能で kor an が用いられ、同時的接続詞化辞も kane ではなく kor である。

entailment.quote: Other dialects, such as for instance the Saru dialect, have kor an in a function corresponding to that of kane an in the Shizunai dialect, and the contemporal conjunctionalizer in these dialects is also kor instead of kane

anchor.exact: The verb suffixes -kosanpa and -ekatta may be said to indicate the momentary or instantaneous mode

statement.en: The verb suffixes -kosanpa and -ekatta indicate momentary or instantaneous mode of action.
statement.ja: 動詞接尾辞 -kosanpa および -ekatta は、瞬間的または即時的な動作様態を示す。

entailment.quote: The verb suffixes -kosanpa and -ekatta may be said to indicate the momentary or instantaneous mode

anchor.exact: the plural suffix -pa sometimes serves in an iterative function

statement.en: The plural suffix -pa sometimes serves in an iterative function.
statement.ja: 複数接尾辞 -pa は反復の機能で機能することがある。

entailment.quote: the plural suffix -pa sometimes serves in an iterative function

anchor.exact: the iterative mode may be expressed with the help of the conjunctionalizer ranke

statement.en: The iterative mode of action can be expressed with the conjunctionalizer ranke.
statement.ja: 反復の動作様態は接続詞化辞 ranke を用いて表現することができる。

entailment.quote: the iterative mode may be expressed with the help of the conjunctionalizer ranke

anchor.exact: another conjunctionalizer, ayne (see 14.12.2), may be interpreted as an expression of the resultative mode of action.

statement.en: The conjunctionalizer ayne can express the resultative mode of action.
statement.ja: 接続詞化辞 ayne は結果の動作様態の表現と解釈することができる。

entailment.quote: another conjunctionalizer, ayne, may be interpreted as an expression of the resultative mode of action

anchor.exact: The auxiliary a marks an action as having a certain duration (see also 14.9.1).

statement.en: The auxiliary a marks an action as having a certain duration.
statement.ja: 助動詞 a は動作がある程度の持続性を持つことを標示する。

entailment.quote: The auxiliary a marks an action as having a certain duration

anchor.exact: Usually the verb form with a is repeated, and a nuance of impatience on the part of the speaker is often implied.

statement.en: The verb form followed by the durative particle a is usually repeated, which often implies a nuance of impatience on the part of the speaker.
statement.ja: a を伴う動詞形は通常反復され、話者の側の焦燥感のニュアンスを含意することが多い。

entailment.quote: Usually the verb form with a is repeated, and a nuance of impatience on the part of the speaker is often implied.

anchor.exact: The expression (verb) a (verb) a is often followed by the conjunctionalizer ayne (in which case the final a is sometimes dropped), to indicate that the (too) long duration of something has finally come to an end

statement.en: The repeated expression (verb) a (verb) a is often followed by the conjunctionalizer ayne to indicate that the long duration of something has finally ended and something else will follow.
statement.ja: 反復表現「(動詞) a (動詞) a」の後にはしばしば接続小辞 ayne が続き、何かの（過度に）長い継続がついに終わり、その後に別のことが続くことを示す。

entailment.quote: The expression (verb) a (verb) a is often followed by the conjunctionalizer ayne ..., to indicate that the (too) long duration of something has finally come to an end, and then/now something else will follow.

anchor.exact: in which case the final a is sometimes dropped

statement.en: When (verb) a (verb) a is followed by ayne, the final a is sometimes dropped.
statement.ja: 「(動詞) a (動詞) a」の後に ayne が続く場合、最後の a は脱落することがある。

entailment.quote: The expression (verb) a (verb) a is often followed by the conjunctionalizer ayne (in which case the final a is sometimes dropped)

anchor.exact: When the form (verb) a (verb) a is used with a verb of instantaneous, momentary, or resultative content, i.e. a verb which for semantic reasons can have no duration, a denotes the repetition of an act.

statement.en: When (verb) a (verb) a is used with a verb of instantaneous, momentary, or resultative content, a denotes the repetition of an act (iterative mode of action).
statement.ja: 瞬間的、一時的、または結果的な意味内容を持つ動詞（意味論的理由により継続し得ない動詞）とともに (動詞) a (動詞) a が用いられる場合、a は行為の反復（反復様態）を表す。

conditions: with a verb of instantaneous, momentary, or resultative content

entailment.quote: When the form (verb) a (verb) a is used with a verb of instantaneous, momentary, or resultative content... a denotes the repetition of an act.

anchor.exact: In the Saru dialect ranke is the iterative auxiliary (Tamura: 1960: 349)

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, ranke is an iterative auxiliary, according to Tamura (1960).
statement.ja: 田村（1960）によれば、沙流方言において ranke は反復の補助動詞である。

entailment.quote: In the Saru dialect ranke is the iterative auxiliary (Tamura: 1960: 349)

anchor.exact: ranke is also used in an iterative function in the Shizunai dialect; but this ranke does not belong to the class of auxiliaries — it is a conjunctionalizer

statement.en: In the Shizunai dialect, ranke is used in an iterative function, but it belongs to the class of conjunctionalizers rather than auxiliaries.
statement.ja: 静内方言において ranke は反復の機能で用いられるが、補助動詞ではなく接続小辞の類に属する。

entailment.quote: ranke is also used in an iterative function in the Shizunai dialect; but this ranke does not belong to the class of auxiliaries — it is a conjunctionalizer

anchor.exact: Yet another way of expressing that something goes beyond what is reasonable or expected is through the auxiliary kaspa⁵⁶.

statement.en: Excess of an action, state, or event going beyond what is reasonable or expected can be expressed by the auxiliary kaspa.
statement.ja: 妥当または予期される限度を超える行為・状態・事象の過度（過度様態）は、補助動詞 kaspa によって表現できる。

entailment.quote: Yet another way of expressing that something goes beyond what is reasonable or expected is through the auxiliary kaspa

anchor.exact: The opposite of the excessive mode is the defective mode, which indicates that a process has not been carried through as expected or hoped for, that something is lacking. This is expressed by the auxiliaries niwkes and orakse.

statement.en: The defective mode of action, indicating that a process has not been carried through as expected or hoped for, is expressed by the auxiliaries niwkes and orakse.
statement.ja: 過程が期待通りあるいは希望通りに遂行されず何かが欠けていることを示す欠陥様態は、補助動詞 niwkes および orakse によって表現される。

entailment.quote: The opposite of the excessive mode is the defective mode, which indicates that a process has not been carried through as expected or hoped for, that something is lacking. This is expressed by the auxiliaries niwkes and orakse.

anchor.exact: Niwkes simply indicates that part of a process has been left undone, although it should have been done, but orakse furthermore adds a nuance of dissatisfaction or lack of fulfilment: the part that is lacking is a source of discomfort for the subject.

statement.en: The auxiliary niwkes indicates that part of a process has been left undone, whereas orakse adds a nuance of dissatisfaction or lack of fulfillment that is a source of discomfort for the subject.
statement.ja: 補助動詞 niwkes は過程の一部がなされるべきであったのになされないまま残されていることを単に示し、orakse はさらに不満や満たされないニュアンス（欠けている部分が主語にとって不快感の源であること）を加える。

entailment.quote: Niwkes simply indicates that part of a process has been left undone... but orakse furthermore adds a nuance of dissatisfaction or lack of fulfilment: the part that is lacking is a source of discomfort for the subject.

anchor.exact: The auxiliaries moyre and tunas serve respectively to characterize a process as either slow or quick.

statement.en: The auxiliaries moyre and tunas characterize a process as either slow or quick, respectively.
statement.ja: 補助動詞 moyre と tunas は、過程をそれぞれ遅いか速いかとして特徴づける。

entailment.quote: The auxiliaries moyre and tunas serve respectively to characterize a process as either slow or quick.

anchor.exact: Verbs of movement which contain an indication of direction may - with the interpolation of the coordinative conjunctionalizer wa - be used as auxiliaries to action verbs to describe their direction.

statement.en: Verbs of movement indicating direction may be used as directional auxiliaries to action verbs with the interpolation of the coordinative conjunctionalizer wa.
statement.ja: 方向の指示を含む移動動詞は、並列接続小辞 wa を介挿することで、行為動詞の方向を表す補助動詞として用いられ得る。

conditions: with the interpolation of the coordinative conjunctionalizer wa

entailment.quote: Verbs of movement which contain an indication of direction may - with the interpolation of the coordinative conjunctionalizer wa - be used as auxiliaries to action verbs to describe their direction.

anchor.exact: Ek and arki denote an action directed towards the speaker's position at the moment of speaking, while oman / paye indicate that the action is directed away from the speaker at the moment of speaking.

statement.en: The directional auxiliary pair wa ek (sg.) / wa arki (pl.) denotes an action directed towards the speaker's position at the moment of speaking, while wa oman (sg.) / wa paye (pl.) denotes an action directed away from the speaker.
statement.ja: 方向補助動詞の対 wa ek（単数）/ wa arki（複数）は発話時の話者の位置へ向かう動作を示し、wa oman（単数）/ wa paye（複数）は話者から離れる方向の動作を示す。

entailment.quote: Ek and arki denote an action directed towards the speaker's position at the moment of speaking, while oman / paye indicate that the action is directed away from the speaker at the moment of speaking.

anchor.exact: Other verbs of directed movement, such as san, "descend", or yan, "land", etc. may also be used as directional auxiliaries.

statement.ja: san「下る」や yan「上陸する」などの他の方向性移動動詞も、方向補助動詞として用いられ得る。

entailment.quote: Other verbs of directed movement, such as san, "descend", or yan, "land", etc. may also be used as directional auxiliaries.

anchor.exact: Wa ek may also be used to describe the onset of an action or an event, i.e. with an inchoative meaning.

statement.en: Wa ek may be used with an inchoative meaning to describe the onset of an action or event.
statement.ja: wa ek は行為や事象の開始を表す起動様態の意味でも用いられ得る。

entailment.quote: Wa ek may also be used to describe the onset of an action or an event, i.e. with an inchoative meaning.

anchor.exact: In other dialects the inchoative mode of action may be expressed by the auxiliaries oasi58 or heasi59, but these forms do not appear in my material.

statement.ja: 他方言において起動様態を表す補助動詞 oasi または heasi は、著者の静内方言資料には現れない。

entailment.quote: In other dialects the inchoative mode of action may be expressed by the auxiliaries oasi58 or heasi59, but these forms do not appear in my material.

anchor.exact: The auxiliaries moyre and tunas serve respectively to characterize a process as either slow or quick.

statement.ja: 補助動詞 moyre と tunas はそれぞれ、過程が遅いこと、あるいは速いことを表す。

entailment.quote: The auxiliaries moyre and tunas serve respectively to characterize a process as either slow or quick.

anchor.exact: Verbs of movement which contain an indication of direction may - with the interpolation of the coordinative conjunctionalizer wa - be used as auxiliaries to action verbs to describe their direction.

statement.en: Verbs of movement that indicate direction can, with the interpolation of the coordinative conjunctionalizer wa, be used as auxiliaries to action verbs to describe their direction.
statement.ja: 方向指示を含む移動動詞は、並列接続詞 wa を挟むことで、動作動詞の補助動詞としてその方向を表すために用いられうる。

entailment.quote: Verbs of movement which contain an indication of direction may - with the interpolation of the coordinative conjunctionalizer wa - be used as auxiliaries to action verbs to describe their direction.

anchor.exact: Ek and arki denote an action directed towards the speaker's position at the moment of speaking, while oman / paye indicate that the action is directed away from the speaker at the moment of speaking.

statement.en: Ek and arki denote an action directed towards the speaker's position at speech time, whereas oman and paye indicate that the action is directed away from the speaker.

statement.ja: san（下る）や yan（上陸する）などの他の有向移動動詞も、方向の補助動詞として用いられうる。

anchor.exact: In other dialects the inchoative mode of action may be expressed by the auxiliaries oasi58 or heasi59, but these forms do not appear in my material.

anchor.exact: Imperative sentences differ from declarative ones by the dropping of the pronominal affix attached to the verb:

statement.en: Imperative sentences differ from declarative ones by dropping the pronominal affix attached to the verb.

entailment.quote: There is only one concessive conjunctionalizer, namely yakka

entailment.quote: the coordinative conjunctionalizer hike, followed by the restrictive postposition ka, also has a concessive function.

entailment.quote: Yakka is probably a combination of the conditional conjunctionalizer yak (14.12.6) and the restrictive postposition ka.

anchor.exact:
where the construction

(sentence) yakka pirka

means "it is all right that you..." or "you may..."

anchor.exact: The Shizunai dialect has three such conjunctionalizers, namely cik, yakun, and yak.

statement.en: The Shizunai dialect has three conditional conjunctionalizers: cik, yakun, and yak.
statement.ja: 静内方言にはcik、yakun、yakという3つの条件接続語がある。

entailment.quote: The Shizunai dialect has three such conjunctionalizers, namely cik, yakun, and yak.

anchor.exact: Cik is rather infrequently used.

statement.en: The conditional conjunctionalizer cik is rather infrequently used.
statement.ja: 条件接続語cikはあまり頻繁には用いられない。

entailment.quote: Cik is rather infrequently used.

anchor.exact: In stories it mostly appears in fixed expressions, where its meaning overlaps with that of the consequential conjunctionalizers⁷⁾.

statement.en: In stories, cik mostly appears in fixed expressions where its meaning overlaps with that of consequential conjunctionalizers.

entailment.quote: In stories it mostly appears in fixed expressions, where its meaning overlaps with that of the consequential conjunctionalizers.

anchor.exact: In the colloquial language cik is used in connection with imperative statements, where the conjunctionalized sentence expresses the assumption upon which the command or suggestion in the final predicate is based.

statement.en: In colloquial speech, cik is used in connection with imperative statements, where the subordinate clause expresses the assumption upon which the command or suggestion in the final predicate is based.
statement.ja: 口語においてcikは命令表現に関連して用いられ、接続節は末尾の述語における命令や提言の根拠となる前提を表す。

entailment.quote: In the colloquial language cik is used in connection with imperative statements, where the conjunctionalized sentence expresses the assumption upon which the command or suggestion in the final predicate is based.

anchor.exact: Cik may also be used in ordinary conditional expressions when the condition is hypothetical.

statement.en: The conjunctionalizer cik may also be used in ordinary conditional expressions when the condition is hypothetical.
statement.ja: 接続語cikは、条件が仮定的である場合、通常の条件表現にも用いることができる。

entailment.quote: Cik may also be used in ordinary conditional expressions when the condition is hypothetical.

anchor.exact: The Saru dialect has the frequently used conjunctionalizer, ciki, which in meaning and function corresponds more closely to yakun in the Shizunai dialect

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, the conjunctionalizer ciki corresponds in meaning and function to yakun in the Shizunai dialect.
statement.ja: 沙流方言において、頻繁に用いられる接続詞化辞cikiは、静内方言のyakunに意味と機能の点でより密接に対応する。

entailment.quote: The Saru dialect has the frequently used conjunctionalizer, ciki, which in meaning and function corresponds more closely to yakun in the Shizunai dialect.

anchor.exact: Yakun indicates that the speaker does not know whether the statement made in the conjunctionalized sentence is actually going to be realized or not, but if it is realized, the contents of the following sentence will become relevant.

statement.en: The conjunctionalizer yakun indicates that the speaker does not know whether the statement in the subordinate clause will be realized, but if realized, the following sentence becomes relevant.
statement.ja: 接続詞化辞yakunは、従属節で述べられた内容が実際に実現するかどうか話者には不明であるが、もし実現した場合には後続文の内容が妥当となることを示す。

entailment.quote: Yakun indicates that the speaker does not know whether the statement made in the conjunctionalized sentence is actually going to be realized or not, but if it is realized, the contents of the following sentence will become relevant.

anchor.exact: As in some of the constructions with cik, the following predicate often expresses an order, a wish, or a suggestion.

statement.en: Following a clause marked by yakun, the main predicate often expresses an order, a wish, or a suggestion.
statement.ja: yakunで接続詞化された節に続く述語は、命令、願望、または提案を表すことが多い。

entailment.quote: As in some of the constructions with cik, the following predicate often expresses an order, a wish, or a suggestion.

anchor.exact: Yakun also appears in subjunctive constructions with pirka, "be fine"

statement.en: The conjunctionalizer yakun appears in subjunctive expressions in combination with pirka 'be fine'.
statement.ja: 接続詞化辞yakunは、pirka（良い）と組み合わさって仮定・願望構文に現れる。

entailment.quote: Yakun also appears in subjunctive constructions with pirka, "be fine":

anchor.exact: Finally, yakun may appear in ordinary conditional constructions, where the second sentence depends upon or necessarily follows upon the conjunctionalized sentence. In the latter case yakun carries a nuance of "when", so that the conditional meaning is overlaid with temporal implications.

statement.en: In ordinary conditional constructions where the apodosis necessarily follows from the protasis, yakun carries a nuance of 'when' with temporal implications.
statement.ja: 後続節が接続詞化された節に依存するか必然的に続く通常の条件構文において、yakunは「〜の時」というニュアンスを帯び、時間的含意が重なる。

entailment.quote: In the latter case yakun carries a nuance of "when", so that the conditional meaning is overlaid with temporal implications.

anchor.exact: Yakun is etymologically connected with yak (see below), combined with the attributive/allative postposition, un (see 14.3 and 14.5.2).

statement.en: Yakun is etymologically connected with yak combined with the attributive/allative postposition un.
statement.ja: yakunは語源的にyakと連体・向格後置詞unの結合に関連している。

entailment.quote: Yakun is etymologically connected with yak (see below), combined with the attributive/allative postposition, un

anchor.exact: Yak indicates that if a certain condition is (or is not) present as expressed in the conjunctionalized sentence, the contents expressed in the following sentence will necessarily come about.

statement.en: The conjunctionalizer yak indicates that if a certain condition is present or absent in the subordinate clause, the content of the following sentence will necessarily come about.
statement.ja: 接続詞化辞yakは、従属節で表される特定の条件が存在する（または存在しない）場合、後続文で表される内容が必然的に生じることを示す。

entailment.quote: Yak indicates that if a certain condition is (or is not) present as expressed in the conjunctionalized sentence, the contents expressed in the following sentence will necessarily come about.

anchor.exact: This construction often carries the implication that the speaker fears the realization of the conjunctionalized sentence and mentions the consequences in the following sentence as a kind of warning.

statement.en: Clauses conjoined with yak often imply that the speaker fears the realization of the condition and mentions the consequences as a kind of warning.
statement.ja: yak節構文は、話者がその条件の実現を恐れ、一種の警告として結果に言及しているという含意を伴うことが多い。

entailment.quote: This construction often carries the implication that the speaker fears the realization of the conjunctionalized sentence and mentions the consequences in the following sentence as a kind of warning.

anchor.exact: In this function yak is frequently reinforced by the restrictive postposition, anak.

statement.en: In its warning function, yak is frequently reinforced by the restrictive postposition anak.
statement.ja: 警告の機能において、yakは限定の後置詞anakによって強められることが多い。

entailment.quote: In this function yak is frequently reinforced by the restrictive postposition, anak.

anchor.exact: In rapid speech yak occasionally drops the initial [y].

statement.en: In rapid speech, yak occasionally drops its initial [y].
statement.ja: 早口の談話では、yakは語頭の[y]を脱落させることがある。

entailment.quote: In rapid speech yak occasionally drops the initial [y].

anchor.exact: In contrast to yakun, which often indicates hypothetical conditions, yak generally refers to matters which habitually stand in a conditional relation-

statement.en: Whereas yakun often indicates hypothetical conditions, yak generally refers to matters that habitually stand in a conditional relationship.
statement.ja: yakunが仮定的な条件を示すことが多いのに対し、yakは一般に習慣的に条件関係にある事柄を指す。

entailment.quote: In contrast to yakun, which often indicates hypothetical conditions, yak generally refers to matters which habitually stand in a conditional relation-

anchor.exact: Yak occasionally begins a sentence and thus functions as a free form

anchor.exact: The Saru dialect also has the conjunctionalizer yak, and it is very close in meaning and function to the yak described here (Tamura: 1972-3: 67ff).

entailment.quote: The Saru dialect also has the conjunctionalizer yak, and it is very close in meaning and function to the yak described here (Tamura: 1972-3: 67ff).

anchor.exact: The Shizunai dialect has only one such morpheme, namely korka

statement.en: The Shizunai dialect has only one adversative conjunctionalizer morpheme, namely korka.
statement.ja: 静内方言には逆接の接続語化形態素として korka のただ1つのみが存在する。

statement.ja: 等位接続語化辞 hike は限定後置詞 ka を伴うことで逆接の標識としても機能しうる。

entailment.quote: the coordinative conjunctionalizer hike (14.12.1), reinforced by the restrictive postposition ka, may also function as a marker of adverseness.

anchor.exact: Korka is found in all Hokkaidō dialects of Ainu (Hattori: 1964:323)

statement.ja: 逆接の接続語化辞 korka はアイヌ語のすべての北海道方言に見られる。

entailment.quote: Korka is found in all Hokkaidō dialects of Ainu (Hattori: 1964:323)

anchor.exact: not in the Sakhalin Raychishka dialect.

entailment.quote: but not in the Sakhalin Raychishka dialect.

anchor.exact: It indicates that the contents of the second of the two sentences which it connects occur contrary to expectation and in opposition to the conjunctionalized sentence.

statement.en: The conjunctionalizer korka indicates that the contents of the second connected clause occur contrary to expectation and in opposition to the conjunctionalized clause.
statement.ja: 接続語化辞 korka は、それが接続する2つの文のうち後続節の内容が予想に反し、接続節と対立して生起することを示す。

entailment.quote: It indicates that the contents of the second of the two sentences which it connects occur contrary to expectation and in opposition to the conjunctionalized sentence.

anchor.exact: The ka of korka may be interpreted as the restrictive postposition ka, added to kor, which is the contemporal conjunctionalizer in e.g. the Saru dialect.

anchor.exact: Any complete sentence in Ainu may be either adnominalized (by being put in front of a noun) or nominalized (by being put in front of a nominalizer).

statement.en: Any complete sentence in Ainu may be either adnominalized by being placed before a noun or nominalized by being placed before a nominalizer.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の任意の完全文は、名詞の直前に置かれることで連体修飾節化されるか、または名詞化辞の直前に置かれることで名詞化されうる。

entailment.quote: Any complete sentence in Ainu may be either adnominalized (by being put in front of a noun) or nominalized (by being put in front of a nominalizer).

anchor.exact: Nominalizers are noun-like words, which may occur only with adnominal modification.

statement.en: Nominalizers in Ainu are noun-like bound words that can only occur with adnominal modification.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の名詞化辞は、連体修飾を伴ってのみ生起しうる名詞的な結合形式である。

entailment.quote: Nominalizers are noun-like words, which may occur only with adnominal modification.

anchor.exact: While conjunctionalized sentences become adverbial adjuncts (see 15.6), nominalized sentences become relational adjuncts (see 15.5)

statement.ja: 接続節化された文は副詞的付加語となるのに対し、名詞化された文は関係的付加語となる。

entailment.quote: While conjunctionalized sentences become adverbial adjuncts (see 15.6), nominalized sentences become relational adjuncts (see 15.5)

anchor.exact: although both may be followed by restrictive postpositions, only nominalized sentences may be followed by case postpositions.

statement.ja: 接続節化された文と名詞化された文はともに限定後置詞を後続させうるが、格後置詞を後続させることができるのは名詞化された文だけである。

entailment.quote: although both may be followed by restrictive postpositions, only nominalized sentences may be followed by case postpositions.

anchor.exact: nominalized adjuncts are rarely marked with case postpositions

anchor.exact: In the majority of cases hi follows verbs which have to do with speaking or listening.

statement.ja: 大半の場合、名詞化辞hiは「話す」または「聞く」ことに関する動詞の後に続く。

statement.en: The nominalizer hi is used in the formation of some personal pronouns.
statement.ja: 名詞化辞hiは一部の人称代名詞の形成にも用いられる。

entailment.quote: Hi is also the nominalizer used in forming some of the personal pronouns

anchor.exact: Pe is mostly used for unspecified concrete things or persons, but it may also be used about abstract matters like hi.

statement.en: The nominalizer pe is mostly used for unspecified concrete things or persons, but it may also refer to abstract matters like hi.
statement.ja: 名詞化辞peは主に不特定の具体物や人を表すのに用いられるが、hiのように抽象的な事柄を表すこともある。

entailment.quote: Pe may also be modified by demonstrative pronouns as in taan pe, 'this thing/guy'

entailment.quote: Adjuncts, which are neither subject, nor object; which are not marked with case postpositions or can be interpreted as instances of ellipsis of case postpositions; and which are furthermore not quotations, are regarded as adverbial adjuncts

anchor.exact: an adverbial adjunct may consist of either a conjunction (12.6.1), an interjection (12.6.2), an adverb (12.6.3), or a conjunctionalized sentence (14.12)

statement.en: An adverbial adjunct may consist of a conjunction, an interjection, an adverb, or a conjunctionalized sentence.
statement.ja: 副詞的付加語は、接続詞、間投詞、副詞、または接続詞化された文のいずれかから構成されうる。

entailment.quote: an adverbial adjunct may consist of either a conjunction (12.6.1), an interjection (12.6.2), an adverb (12.6.3), or a conjunctionalized sentence (14.12).

anchor.exact: Like the relational adjuncts, it may in some cases be followed by a restrictive postposition (14.6).

statement.en: An adverbial adjunct may in some cases be followed by a restrictive postposition.
statement.ja: 副詞的付加語は、場合によって限定の後置詞を後続させることができる。

entailment.quote: Like the relational adjuncts, it may in some cases be followed by a restrictive postposition (14.6).

anchor.exact: The sentence or noun expression which necessarily precedes the quotationalizer must be something said, thought, felt, or heard

statement.en: The sentence or noun expression preceding a quotationalizer must represent something said, thought, felt, or heard.
statement.ja: 引用化辞に先行する文または名詞表現は、言われたこと、考えられたこと、感じられたこと、あるいは聞かれたことでなければならない。

entailment.quote: The sentence or noun expression which necessarily precedes the quotationalizer must be something said, thought, felt, or heard

anchor.exact: quotational adjuncts are only found with predicates which have either of these or similar meanings.

statement.en: Quotational adjuncts are found only with predicates expressing speaking, thinking, feeling, hearing, or similar meanings.
statement.ja: 引用付加語は、発言、思考、感情、聴覚などを表す述語、またはそれに類似した意味を持つ述語とのみ生起する。

entailment.quote: quotational adjuncts are only found with predicates which have either of these or similar meanings.

anchor.exact: A minimal noun expression consists of one nominal, which may be a general noun, a proper name, a quantity noun, or a positional.

statement.en: A minimal noun expression consists of a single nominal, which may be a general noun, a proper name, a quantity noun, or a positional.
statement.ja: 最小限の名詞表現は単一の名詞類から構成され、それは普通名詞、固有名詞、数量名詞、または位置名詞でありうる。

entailment.quote: A minimal noun expression consists of one nominal, which may be a general noun, a proper name, a quantity noun, or a positional.

anchor.exact: Positionals, however, more often than not succeed a general noun which establishes the locational reference point

statement.en: Positionals usually follow a general noun that establishes the locational reference point.
statement.ja: 位置名詞は、位置の基準点を設定する普通名詞の後に後続することが通例である。

entailment.quote: Positionals, however, more often than not succeed a general noun which establishes the locational reference point

anchor.exact: Only general nouns may be modified by adnouns or take noun prefixes, pronominal prefixes, or noun suffixes.

statement.en: Only general nouns may be modified by adnouns or take noun prefixes, pronominal prefixes, or noun suffixes.
statement.ja: 連体詞によって修飾されたり、名詞接頭辞、人称接頭辞、名詞接尾辞を取ることができるのは普通名詞だけである。

entailment.quote: Only general nouns may be modified by adnouns or take noun prefixes, pronominal prefixes, or noun suffixes.

anchor.exact: Adnouns and pronominal prefixes are mutually exclusive; if a noun is determined by one of the four types of adnouns (see 14.1.1), it cannot be pronominally determined as well — and vice versa

statement.en: Adnouns and pronominal prefixes on a general noun are mutually exclusive.
statement.ja: 普通名詞において連体詞と代名詞的接頭辞は相互排他的である。

entailment.quote: Adnouns and pronominal prefixes are mutually exclusive; if a noun is determined by one of the four types of adnouns, it cannot be pronominally determined as well — and vice versa

anchor.exact: noun expressions may be linked together, either by just enumerating them (this mostly happens with general nouns), or by inserting an attributive or coordinative postposition.

statement.en: Noun expressions may be linked together by mere juxtaposition or enumeration, which occurs mostly with general nouns.
statement.ja: 名詞表現は単なる並置や列挙によって結合されることがあり、これは主に普通名詞で生じる。

entailment.quote: noun expressions may be linked together, either by just enumerating them (this mostly happens with general nouns)

anchor.exact: In the case of coordinative linking, the coordinative postposition is often repeated after each noun expression

statement.en: In coordinative linking of noun expressions, the coordinative postposition is often repeated after each noun expression.
statement.ja: 名詞表現の等位結合では、等位後置詞がそれぞれの名詞表現の後に繰り返されることが多い。

entailment.quote: the coordinative postposition is often repeated after each noun expression
